p|panel|rv_t_defender_nube: What Microsoft Defender sends to the cloud
p|panel|rv_t_aprovisionados: Apps Windows installs in every new account
p|panel|rv_nd: Windows did not say in this check-up.
p|panel|rv_actualizaciones_apagadas: Automatic updates are turned off. Without them, known security holes stay open.
p|panel|rv_actualizaciones_viejas: The last update was installed {n} days ago. Open Windows Update and check for updates.
p|panel|rv_actualizaciones_pausadas: Updates are paused for {dias} more days.
p|panel|rv_actualizaciones_reinicio: Updates are waiting for a restart to finish.
p|panel|rv_actualizaciones_ok: The last update was installed {n} days ago. To know whether any are pending, open Windows Update.
p|panel|rv_antivirus_ninguno: Windows sees no antivirus turned on.
p|panel|rv_antivirus_viejo: An antivirus is on but not up to date.
p|panel|rv_defender_manipulacion: Tamper protection is off: another program could turn Defender off.
p|panel|rv_defender_ok: Active, with signatures {n} days old and tamper protection.
p|panel|rv_defender_pasivo: Defender is on standby: another antivirus protects.
p|panel|rv_cortafuegos_apagado: Off for some network: the list says which.
p|panel|rv_uac_apagado: Off: any program can make administrator changes without asking you.
p|panel|rv_uac_ok: On: Windows asks before administrator changes.
p|panel|rv_smb1_activo: Enabled. It is the protocol WannaCry used; almost nobody needs it now.
p|panel|rv_arranque_seguro_ok: On: the computer only boots signed software.
p|panel|rv_arranque_seguro_sin_uefi: This computer boots in old BIOS mode and does not have it.
p|panel|rv_cifrado_ok: Drive {unidad} is encrypted: if the computer is stolen, it cannot be read.
p|panel|rv_cifrado_no: Drive {unidad} is not encrypted: whoever takes the computer can read the disk.
p|panel|rv_cifrado_nd: This Windows edition does not report encryption.
p|panel|rv_integridad_ok: On: harder to load malicious drivers.
p|panel|rv_cuentas_aviso: {n} active accounts, {admins} administrators. Something in the list needs a look ({creadas} created in 30 days).
p|panel|rv_cuentas_ok: {n} active accounts, {admins} administrators. None new or without password.
p|panel|rv_rdp_sin_nla: On and without prior authentication: the most attacked door.
p|panel|rv_rdp_activo: On: this computer can be entered from another. Such sign-ins in 30 days: {n}.
p|panel|rv_asistencia_activa: Allowed: someone you invite can see or control your screen.
p|panel|rv_acceso_remoto_hay: There are {n}. Useful, and also the first thing a fake “tech support” asks for: if you did not install it, remove it.
p|panel|rv_fallidos: {n} failed passwords in 7 days: someone or something is trying.
p|panel|rv_autologon_clave: The computer signs in on its own and keeps the password unprotected in the registry.
p|panel|rv_autologon: The computer signs in on its own, without a password.
p|panel|rv_puertos_delicados: Programs are listening on ports used to control the computer remotely.
p|panel|rv_puertos_ok: Only Windows listens on the network.
p|panel|rv_puertos_hay: {n} programs that are not Windows wait for connections from your local network (that does not mean internet can reach them; the firewall decides).
p|panel|rv_compartido_hay: You share {n} folders on the network.
p|panel|rv_inventario: {n} in total · {nuevos} new · {raros} without a valid signature or file.
p|panel|rv_dns_falsea: Your DNS gives unexpected answers for well-known names. It may be your provider's filter or a diversion: check which DNS the router uses.
p|panel|rv_dns_redirige: Your DNS answers with an address when the name does not exist: your provider redirects errors (often to ads).
p|panel|rv_dns_ok: Tested: it tells the truth and does not make up addresses.
p|panel|rv_dns_sin_prueba: Could not be tested (the DNS is GUARDIANA on this computer or did not answer).
p|panel|rv_proxy_ok: No proxy: your traffic goes direct.
p|panel|rv_proxy_hay: Your web traffic goes through a proxy. If you (or your company) did not set it, it may read or divert your browsing.
p|panel|rv_vpn_si: Your internet goes out through a VPN.
p|panel|rv_hosts_redirige: {n} names diverted by hand. If you did not do it, it is a classic trick to send you to fake sites.
p|panel|rv_hosts_bloquea: {n} names blocked (some ad blockers do this).
p|panel|rv_certificados_ok: Only Windows ones and its official program ({n} in total).
p|panel|rv_certificados_hay: {n} outside Microsoft's automatic program. Includes some Windows factory ones and those added by antivirus or companies to inspect encrypted traffic. The list says which.
p|panel|rv_wifi_viejo: Old encryption ({tipo}): easily broken. Set the router to WPA2 or WPA3.
p|panel|rv_wifi_nd: Windows did not say the encryption type.
p|panel|rv_wifi_abierta: Unencrypted network ({tipo}): anyone nearby can see what is not encrypted.
p|panel|rv_perfil_privada: Network marked private: the computer is visible to others on it.
p|panel|rv_perfil_publica: Network marked public: the computer stays hidden.
p|panel|rv_uso_ahora: A program has not released it: it may be in use now. {n} programs have used it (Windows keeps the last time of each).
p|panel|rv_uso_hay: {n} programs have used it; Windows keeps the last time of each.
p|panel|rv_telemetria_opcional: Optional diagnostic data: the most Windows sends. Change it in Settings > Privacy > Diagnostics.
p|panel|rv_telemetria_sin_fijar: Not set: whatever was chosen when installing Windows.
p|panel|rv_publicidad_si: On: apps can recognize you for advertising.
p|panel|rv_fabricante_hay: {n} maker or trial programs that came with the computer. The “Live globe” shows how much each one sends.
p|panel|rv_usb: {n} USB drives or disks according to Windows.
p|panel|rv_bios_vieja: The firmware is {n} years old: check whether the maker has a newer one.
p|panel|rv_amenazas_hay: {n} detections in 7 days: the list says which and what it did.
p|panel|rv_analisis: {analisis} scans finished and {firmas} signature updates in 7 days.
p|panel|rv_tiempo_real_apagado: Real-time protection was turned off {n} times in 7 days.
p|panel|rv_exclusiones_no: None: Defender has no folders, programs or file types excluded from scanning.
p|panel|rv_exclusiones_hay: {n} exclusions: Defender does not scan what is on this list (for an excluded program, the files that program opens). If neither you nor your organization added them, review them in Windows Security: adding exclusions is a known technique of malicious programs.
p|panel|rv_lsa_ok: On: at the last startup, Windows started LSA as a protected process, which makes it harder to steal credentials from memory.
p|panel|rv_lsa_no: It did not start protected at the last startup. On Windows 11, turn it on in Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation.
p|panel|rv_servicios_remotos_no: None running: no OpenSSH, no WinRM, no Remote Registry.
p|panel|rv_servicios_remotos_hay: {n} running. They let another computer operate or query this one if they are set up for it. If you do not need them, it is best to stop them.
p|panel|rv_gestion_no: No organization: the computer is not joined to a domain or to Microsoft Entra, nor enrolled in device management.
p|panel|rv_gestion_si: An organization manages this computer: it can install programs and change settings remotely. If this is a personal computer and you did not expect it, find out who enrolled it.
p|panel|rv_pantalla_nunca: Windows has no program recorded capturing the screen through its official route. Captures made any other way are not recorded.
p|panel|rv_pantalla_hay: {n} programs have captured the screen through Windows' official route; the last time of each is kept. Captures made any other way are not recorded.
p|panel|rv_pantalla_ahora: A program has not finished its capture: it may be capturing the screen now. {n} programs have captured it through Windows' official route.
p|panel|rv_diagtrack_activo: Running: this is the service that sends Windows' diagnostic data to Microsoft.
p|panel|rv_diagtrack_parado: Stopped now, though it can start again.
p|panel|rv_nube_apagada: Cloud protection is off: Defender does not ask Microsoft about suspicious files and loses the cloud's fast protection against new threats.
p|panel|rv_nube_seguras: It asks Microsoft about suspicious files and sends, without asking, samples of those that do not usually contain personal data (programs such as .exe or .dll); if a file may contain it, it asks first. This is the factory setting.
p|panel|rv_nube_todas: It asks Microsoft about suspicious files and automatically sends samples of any file, including documents that may contain personal data.
p|panel|rv_nube_pregunta: It asks Microsoft about suspicious files and asks you before sending any sample.
p|panel|rv_nube_nunca: It asks Microsoft about suspicious files but does not send samples of your files. Microsoft states that it still receives data about each detection.
p|panel|rv_recall_sin_capturas: A policy prevents Recall from saving snapshots of the screen.
p|panel|rv_recall_instalado: Recall is installed. It only saves periodic snapshots of the screen if someone turns it on in Settings; GUARDIANA cannot read whether anyone did.
p|panel|rv_recall_apagado: The Recall component is turned off.
p|panel|rv_aprovisionados_no: None from other companies, apart from Microsoft's and the computer maker's.
p|panel|rv_asr_activas: {n} rules block typical attack techniques (Office macros, obfuscated scripts, credential theft…) and {a} only log them.
p|panel|rv_asr_auditoria: {n} rules are in audit mode: they log attack techniques but do not stop them.
p|panel|rv_asr_ninguna: No rule is active. They are an extra layer of Microsoft Defender; at home they are set with administration tools.
p|panel|rv_red_ok: On: Defender stops connections to sites known for scams or malicious programs from any program, not only from the browser.
p|panel|rv_red_auditoria: In audit mode: it logs dangerous connections but does not stop them.
p|panel|rv_red_no: Off: only the browser warns about dangerous sites; other programs can connect to them.
p|panel|rv_pua_ok: On: Windows stops programs that install themselves hidden inside others, add advertising or mine cryptocurrency.
p|panel|rv_pua_auditoria: In audit mode: it logs them but does not stop them.
p|panel|rv_pua_no: Off. Turn it on in Windows Security > App & browser control > Reputation-based protection.
p|panel|rv_carpetas_ok: On: only trusted programs can change your documents, photos and desktop.
p|panel|rv_carpetas_auditoria: In audit mode: it logs who tries to change your folders but does not stop them.
p|panel|rv_carpetas_no: Off. It stops ransomware that wants to encrypt your documents; turn it on in Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Ransomware protection.
p|panel|rv_cg_ok: Running: Windows credentials live isolated, out of reach of programs.
p|panel|rv_cg_no: Not running: it isolates Windows credentials so a malicious program cannot steal them. Not every Windows edition includes it.
p|panel|rv_smartscreen_ok: On: Windows warns before opening downloaded programs and files it does not know.
p|panel|rv_smartscreen_no: Off: Windows opens downloaded programs it does not know without warning. Turn it on in Windows Security > App & browser control.
p|panel|rv_sac_ok: On: Windows only lets signed programs or those with a good reputation run.
p|panel|rv_sac_evaluacion: In evaluation: Windows is watching how you use the computer to decide whether to turn it on.
p|panel|rv_sac_no: Off. On Windows 11 it can only be turned on by reinstalling Windows: it is not a fault, most computers come like this.
p|panel|rv_drivers_ok: On: Windows does not load the drivers Microsoft knows are used to take over the computer.
p|panel|rv_drivers_no: Off: a program could load a driver known to be vulnerable and get past the antivirus. Turn it on in Windows Security > Device security > Core isolation.
p|panel|rv_drivers_nd: Windows does not say whether the list is on; before Windows 11 22H2 it comes off.
p|panel|rv_oculto_ok: Nothing in the less visible startup points (Winlogon, AppInit, IFEO debuggers and WMI subscriptions).
p|panel|rv_oculto_hay: {n} entries in the less visible startup points, the ones malicious programs use to hide. Some are set by legitimate programs: if you do not know what they are, ask for help before touching them.
p|panel|rv_udp_ok: No program other than Windows waits for UDP connections from the network.
p|panel|rv_udp_hay: {n} programs other than Windows wait for UDP messages from the network (calls, games, shared music…). If one does not ring a bell, check what it is.
p|panel|rv_entrada_ok: No program has its own exception to receive connections through the firewall.
p|panel|rv_entrada_hay: {n} exceptions let connections in to specific programs; they are created when you click «Allow access» on the firewall prompt.
p|panel|rv_smb_firma_ok: Shared folders require signing both ways: nobody in between can change what travels.
p|panel|rv_smb_firma_no: Shared folders do not always require signing: on someone else's network, someone in between could alter what travels. Windows 11 24H2 requires it by default.
p|panel|rv_doh_si: Windows encrypts its DNS questions (DNS over HTTPS) on {n} connections.
p|panel|rv_doh_no: Windows has no DNS over HTTPS set up: its DNS questions go out unencrypted, unless another program encrypts them.
p|panel|rv_nrpt_hay: {n} rules send certain names to specific DNS servers. Company VPNs and some programs use them; if you have none, check where they come from.
p|panel|rv_llmnr_ok: Off: this computer does not answer local network names over LLMNR or NetBIOS.
p|panel|rv_llmnr_activo: This computer asks for and answers local network names over LLMNR or NetBIOS. Handy at home; on public Wi-Fi, another computer can pose as a server to ask for your password.
p|panel|rv_aprovisionados_hay: {n} apps from other companies come in this computer's Windows image and install themselves in every new account.
p|panel|rv_marca_en_uso: not closed: maybe in use now
p|panel|rv_certificados_nuevo: {n} new root certificates since the first check-up. With one, a program can read your encrypted traffic: if you do not know where they come from, check it.

p|panel|rv_vivo_s_sistema: firewall, UAC, Secure Boot, TPM and encryption

p|panel|pd_lugar_zona_aviso: Your computer is placed by its time zone, in {lugar}. If that is not your city, correct it or measure with GPS or Wi-Fi: it stays in this browser only.
p|panel|pd_ht_buscar: Search program, destination, company, country, network…
p|panel|rd_titulo: Checking your computer, piece by piece
p|panel|rd_firmas_frase: {ok} validly signed · {sin} without a valid signature
